subject: Post-demo: model fit & Redwood-verified benchmarks for Acme AI
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: model fit & Redwood-verified benchmarks for Acme AI

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + recommended next steps based on the use cases you described (customer support triage + short-form summarization):

Summary of fit:
- Primary recommendation: gptx-6b-quantized (cost-efficient, good zero-shot summarization quality on short sequences).
- Fallback for latency-sensitive chat flows: gptx-2.7b-lowlatency (lower context overhead, better p95 latency at small batch sizes).
- Sticky choice for long-context classification/analytics: gptx-13b with 8-bit quant (if you need higher quality on longer transcripts).

Benchmarks & artifacts I attached:
- Redwood-verified performance profile (attached PDF): includes TPS, p50/p90/p95 latency percentiles across the sequence-length distribution you shared.
- eval_prompt_set_v3.jsonl (attached): the short prompt sets we used for the benchmark; please reuse these for your internal qual checks.
- Console links: I also uploaded results to the Console: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/acme-ai-report-20260214

Key numbers (from the verified runs):
- gptx-6b-quantized: 220 TPS (batching), p95 latency = 130 ms for 64-token responses, median latency = 32 ms.
- gptx-2.7b-lowlatency: 380 TPS, p95 latency = 85 ms for 64-token responses, median = 18 ms.
- gptx-13b-8bit: 95 TPS, p95 latency = 420 ms for 256-token responses.

Notes on quality/regression risk:
- We observed occasional phrasing regressions on domain-specific legalese with gptx-6b in 1% of prompts in the eval set. If legal fidelity is critical, recommend validating the specific prompt/response pairs in eval_prompt_set_v3 and considering gptx-13b samples.
- Quantized models show small changes in rare-token generation — we’ve included a delta report in the PDF with example mismatches.

Recommended next steps:
1) Review attached eval prompt set and mark any high-priority prompts (2 business days).
2) I’ll run a targeted canary with your sample transcripts (Ben will help with the ingestion).
3) If the canary looks good, we can recommend a canary-to-production rollout: start on Dedicated for the high-throughput chat path, Hosted for prototype flows.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_benchmarks_acme_20260214.pdf (application/pdf)], [Attachment: eval_prompt_set_v3.jsonl (application/jsonl)]

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & Redwood-verified benchmarks for Acme AI

Thanks Marissa — very helpful. Quick questions after skimming the PDF:
1) For the 220 TPS number on gptx-6b-quantized — is that with prefix caching enabled? Our flows have a lot of repeated context (user profile + product metadata).
2) The 1% regression cases you mentioned: can you surface the exact prompt/response pairs so our legal SME can review?

Also curious on pricing delta if we want to run the canary on Dedicated vs Hosted for 2 weeks (low volume). Happy to loop procurement if needed.

—Sam
Senior Product Manager, Acme AI
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & Redwood-verified benchmarks for Acme AI

Hey Sam — quick answers: 
- The 220 TPS for gptx-6b-quantized was measured with prefix/KV caching enabled (typical for repeated context). Without caching, expect ~28% lower TPS for the same batch profile. I added a short note in the Console report explaining the cache-hit assumptions.
- I extracted the regression samples (see attached small CSV in the PDF appendix). Marissa, I flagged 6 pairs that look like hallucinated statute references — happy to escalate to Applied ML if Acme wants a focused mitigation (prompt scaffolding + post-filtering).

Regarding canary cost: estimated incremental spend for a 2-week low-volume canary (up to 5k requests/day):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go) on gptx-6b-quantized: ~$1,200 — includes streaming and standard bandwidth.
- Dedicated reserved slot (small pool) with burstable credits: prorated ~ $2,500 + small infra setup fee.

If you want, we can start a Hosted canary and if performance/costs look promising, swap to a small Dedicated pool for production.

[Attachment: cost_estimate_acme_canary.csv (text/csv)]

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
